children: Nomura has retained Marico, Tata Consumer and ITC as its top picks in the consumer staples segment, while Lenskart Solutions is among its preferred consumer discretionary stocks, even as it remains watchful of rural demand following a below-normal monsoon.

In its September 30 report, Nomura said the 2026 monsoon season ended with rainfall around 12.5% below normal, higher than the India Meteorological Department’s forecast of a 10% deficit. The brokerage noted that Kharif sowing was down 1.5% year-on-year, with rice and maize sowing declining 3.8% and 2.6%, respectively.

Nomura said higher buffer stocks could help keep inflation in check, but flagged risks from lower reservoir levels for Rabi crops. As of September 24, live storage was 11.5% below the 10-year average.

“We remain watchful of rural demand as we believe that it will likely face multiple headwinds of below-normal monsoon, El Niño, and product price increases being taken by companies due to the West-Asia conflict,” the brokerage said.

Nomura noted that rural growth “has started moderating, converging with urban growth”. It added that while overall inflation and mid-single-digit price increases remain manageable and may not materially pressure volumes for now, further price hikes or an impact on agricultural yields could add to pressure on demand and consumption.
The brokerage also flagged the risk to companies with greater exposure to winter portfolios, including cold creams, lotions and Chyawanprash, amid the possibility of warmer winters due to El Niño.
“We believe given warmer winters due to El Niño, companies with higher winter portfolio (higher margin) exposure could see some moderation in growth and margins,” Nomura said.
It prefers companies with higher urban saliency, pricing power, strong brands, resilient portfolios and better execution.

title: Nomura names Marico, Tata Consumer, ITC top picks as monsoon deficit raises rural demand concerns
